title: Inline column trimming and hover summary for virtual tables
creator: Marisol Vega
description: Problem: In highly virtualized table views, users lose context for column content when columns collapse or are truncated. Current approaches either force wide columns (hurting density) or rely on tooltip-only patterns that break under keyboard navigation and on touch devices. Goal: Design an inline trimming strategy plus a lightweight hover/keyboard-focus summary that preserves density while exposing important content promptly and accessibly. This ticket covers research, a prototype in the sandbox, accessibility requirements, and specs for engineering (CSS + aria) and the component API for the table library.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype implemented in virtualized sandbox with mocked large datasets (10k rows) demonstrating inline trimming with stable layout
Hover summary appears within 200ms on pointer hover and on focus with keyboard; functions with continuous-batching virtualization without forcing rerenders
Accessible: summary is reachable via keyboard, readable by screen readers, and does not interfere with row selection — aria attributes documented
Design tokens and CSS variables defined for truncated indicators, summary background, and animation durations
Engineering API: column property 'summaryOnOverflow' and 'summaryPosition' documented and agreed
Performance: no measurable token-level throughput regression in the perf harness ( <5% p50 rendering time )
Design sign-off from PM and Eng and an initial implementation PR opened
design_notes: Prototype strategy: inline trimming shows an ellipsis and a faint gradient mask to signal overflow; hovering reveals a compact summary card anchored to the cell but constrained inside the viewport
Summary content: prefer first N characters of cell with low-cost heuristics to avoid pulling heavy DOM (avoid innerHTML parsing), fall back to full text when user requests via keyboard toggle
Density trade: native truncation keeps row height consistent; floating summary avoids expanding rows and preserves virtualization assumptions
Touch support: long-press triggers summary when hover not available; must handle scroll cancelation gestures
Animation: fade + translateY(4px) with 120ms duration to feel snappy without jank
Fallback: if KV cache or batching causes delayed content delivery, show instant placeholder summary like 'Loading…' rather than no affordance
decisions: Choose floating summary rather than inline expansion to avoid layout shifts and keep virtualization stable
Expose two props at component API: summaryOnOverflow (boolean) and summaryMode (peek | full); default to peek
Use a low-overhead heuristic to generate summary text on the client; do not request server-side summaries for this feature in initial rollout
Implement keyboard trigger via Alt+Enter on focused cell for screen-reader-friendly explicit expansion
Defer complex filtering of rich content (markdown/images) to a later iteration; initial scope handles plain text and simple HTML stripping
tradeoffs: Pros: preserves density and performance by avoiding row height changes; provides discoverable overflow affordance
Cons: floating summaries add layering complexity and require careful z-index and focus management; touch long-press may conflict with mobile scrolling on very dense tables
Engineering complexity: need to coordinate with virtualization kernel to avoid unnecessary reflows; small risk of clipping on pinned columns that must be handled explicitly
tasks: UX research: run 6 quick sessions to validate discoverability and mental model
Design: create Figma prototype for desktop and a simplified flow for mobile/touch
Accessibility: draft aria pattern and keyboard flow; review with SRE accessibility lead
Engineering: sandbox implementation in 'table-sandbox' branch; unit tests for focus behavior
Perf: add microbenchmark in perf harness and compare p50 render times vs baseline
Docs: update component library docs and examples for summaryOnOverflow API
